detail.longDescription: Typically, I would obtain/return an item from a list of items like so: def search_in_list(search_id): for item in my_list: if item['id'] == search_id: return item return None However, I now stumbled across this code: item = next((item for item in my_list if item["id"] == search_id), None) Which seems to be a condensed version of: for item in my_list: if item["id"] == search_id: break else: item = None Are there any benefits for using the single line or for loop, or a PEP guide which to use when/where? Or is it really just personal preference, maintainability or readability of the code?
